name: JMSFusion
description: Frontend enhancement plugin for Jellyfin Web and web-wrapper mobile clients (Zigerus fork of ParticularFlix JMSFusion, Jellyfin 12). Native Android TV clients are not supported.
overview: Custom script loader for the Jellyfin web UI.

versions.changelog:
### Fixes
- **The home hero no longer stays gone after the page sits open.** Reported: with the home page left open for a while, the hero at the top disappeared and the rows slid up under the header until the page was reloaded. Nothing re-checked the hero once it was gone. The existing health check ran only after a tab change inside home, and the restore repair needs a hero that is still on the page. The trigger could not be reproduced on the test server (tab in front, background tab, the API down across a hero cycle rebuild, window resizes, the Home-tab gate), so the fix does not depend on it:
  - **Hero watchdog.** While the home page is in front, every 10 s, on coming back to the tab, and 9 s and 21 s after each hero cycle rebuild, a hero that should be showing but is missing, hidden or empty twice in a row (4 s apart) is rebuilt in place, keeping the scroll position. It does nothing on the other home tabs (where "Show only on the Home tab" hides the hero on purpose), during a boot or rebuild, while the tab is in the background, or when there is no slide data. It rebuilds at most 3 times in 10 minutes, then logs that it gave up.
  - **Teardown hardening.** The cycle rebuild hides the old hero with an inline `display: none !important` while a spacer holds its place. A hero that survives the reset now gets its display back when it is reused. Three cleanup steps that ran unguarded before the old hero's removal are now guarded, so one of them throwing can no longer leave the hidden hero behind.
  - **What the watchdog found is logged**: to the browser console, to `sessionStorage["jms:heroWatchdogLog"]` (last 20), and to the Jellyfin log through a new signed-in endpoint, `POST /Plugins/JMSFusion/client-log` (at most 20 lines per user per hour, size-capped, control characters removed). Each line holds the hero's state (present, inline/computed display, height, slides, spacer, gate flag), the last teardown and how long ago it ran, the time since the last cycle rebuild, page age, viewport and scroll. If the "only on the Home tab" gate hides the hero while the URL is the Home tab, that is reported once too (the watchdog never overrides the gate).
- Removed the six CSS rules left over from the tag-row drag handles that 4.0.0.94 removed.

### Changes
- **Each tag row has its own place in "Home row order".** The order list at the end of the Home Rows tab shows every tag row by name ("Tag row · Christmas") among the other rows, so one row can sit at the top and another further down. A new row joins the list right after the last tag row (or after Featured Upcoming Movies), renaming a row relabels its entry, and deleting a row removes it, all before saving.
- The saved order stores each row as `tagRow:<row id>`. The section sorter places each row there; rows not placed yet stay where the "Tag rows" group used to sit. The group key that loads all tag rows now sits right before the first placed row, so the rows load where the first one appears.
- The row cards in the editor no longer have drag handles: placement lives in one place, the order list.
- An order saved by 4.0.0.93 (with the single "Tag rows" entry) shows its rows individually at that spot.

### Changes
- **"Top 10 Movies" and "Top 10 Series" show what is popular right now among the titles you haven't watched, and change every day.** The old ranking blended five library queries (TMDb rating twice, newest release, newest added, and the genres of whatever was in progress) and never rotated, so the rows settled on the same highly rated classics until each one was marked watched, and an unrated new title could slip in on newness alone.
- The server now keeps TMDb's `popularity`, `vote_average` and `vote_count` for every movie and show in the library that has a TMDb id (`LibraryPopularityService`, file `tmdb-library-popularity.json`). It fetches one title at a time, 8 in parallel, and refreshes in the background once the data is a day old; a request never waits for it. New signed-in endpoint `GET /Plugins/JMSFusion/library-popularity?type=Movie|Series[&parentIds=…]` lists the numbers for the titles the signed-in user can see.
- The page ranks the user's unwatched films, or the shows they haven't started, by popularity. A show counts as started once any episode is played or in progress. A title needs at least 25 TMDb votes and an average of 6.0 or more, and two versions of one film count once. Each day it draws ten from the top 30, weighted by rank (weight e^(−rank/6)), and shows them in popularity order. The draw is seeded by the user, the row and the local date, so the row is the same all day on every device and different the next day. Over 20,000 simulated days, #1 is in the row 93% of the time, #10 47%, #30 2%, and about six titles carry over from one day to the next.
- The saved list (row cache kind `top_pop`) records the local date it was drawn for and is fresh only on that date and for at most 4 hours.
- With no TMDb key on the server, the rows keep the old ranking. While the server's first fill is still running, they use it for that page load only and save nothing, so the next load asks again. A small library is topped up from the old ranking, but only with unwatched titles that have no TMDb numbers.

### Security
- **Every plugin endpoint now needs a Jellyfin sign-in.** Jellyfin 12 runs with legacy authorization off, so it ignores the `X-Emby-Token` header MonWUI sends and gives the plugin no identity for those requests. Most controllers therefore identified the caller from the `X-Emby-UserId` header or a `userId` query value alone, which anyone can write. An anonymous request carrying an administrator's id could read the Seerr API key, the Sonarr/Radarr settings, the parental-PIN profiles and the request queue, and could reach the admin actions behind the same check. Other endpoints answered with no id at all: the plugin configuration (keys redacted), per-user settings, studio-hub lists, the TMDb trailer cache including `?force=true`, and every user's scoped home-row caches.
- One MVC filter now runs in front of every controller of the plugin, registered globally so a controller added later is closed by default. Identity comes only from something Jellyfin issued: the claims of a validated `Authorization` header or API key, or an `X-Emby-Token` / `X-MediaBrowser-Token` header that matches a signed-in device. Query-string tokens are not honoured. No identity, an unknown token or a disabled user gets 401.
- For a non-administrator, the `X-Emby-UserId` / `X-MediaBrowser-UserId` headers are overwritten with the token's own user, and a `userId` query value naming someone else gets 403. A signed-in user can no longer pose as an administrator. An administrator may still name another user, as the admin pages do.
- Scoped caches (`/Plugins/JMSFusion/ScopedCache/{type}/{server|user}`) refuse a non-administrator a scope that ends in another user's id.
- Only scripts, styles, the custom assets folder, the ping and the studio-hub logo/video files stay public (`[MonwuiPublic]`). The web client loads these before sign-in or through plain tags.
- `RequestAuth`'s levels are unchanged: the configuration endpoint still redacts every key for browser requests.

### Fixes
- The early fetch/XHR wrapper (`runtime/storage-preload.js`) adds the signed-in session's token to plugin requests that carried none: UserSettings, the scoped row caches and the settings window's cache tab. Before sign-in there is no token and the server answers 401, which those callers already handle.

### Changes
- **"Featured Upcoming Movies" shows popular films the signed-in user is likely to want**, not 10 picked at random from the whole TMDb pool. The server now keeps TMDb's `popularity`, `vote_average`, `vote_count` and `genre_ids` for every cached trailer, and when it trims the pool to 150 it keeps the most popular titles. The page scores each film as log-scaled popularity × (0.3 + 0.7 × genre affinity). Affinity is the mean of the film's genre weights, read from the user's own movie library once a day: each played film counts 1, plus 0.5 per rewatch (up to 4) and 2 for a favourite, multiplied by how often the user finishes films of that genre compared with the library as a whole. Each page load draws 5 Coming Soon and 5 In Theaters cards, weighted by score, from the top 12 of each; if one side is short the other fills the gap. With no watch history the row ranks by popularity alone, and a pool cached by an older server keeps the old random pick.

### Fixes
- **The trailer cache no longer refetches everything from TMDb on every request when it holds fewer than 150 trailers.** The 24-hour freshness test also required a full 150, so a region whose lists yield, say, 148 trailers re-ran every list, video and release-date call each time the row or the pre-roll asked. A cache with any trailers is now fresh for 24 hours. A cache written before this version (no popularity on its items) refreshes once; if TMDb is unreachable the old pool is still served.

### Changes
- **English: the "Featured Upcoming Movies" tag for a film already out reads "In Theaters" instead of "Now Playing"** (`tmdbTrailerNowPlayingBadge`), the way the other languages already say it ("Im Kino", "En salle", "Vizyonda"…) and the module's own built-in default. "Now Playing" stays where it means playback (the cast and sync labels).

### Changes
- **The release ribbon on "Featured Upcoming Movies" cards says which state it shows**: `.tmdb-trailer-ribbon` now also carries `tmdb-trailer-ribbon--upcoming` or `tmdb-trailer-ribbon--now-playing` and a matching `data-trailer-state`, so a theme can style Coming Soon and Now Playing apart. The default look does not change.

### Changes
- **English label "Certification" is now "Rating"** (`showOfficialRating`): the pause screen row, the parental-PIN card and the two settings checkboxes that show the official rating (R, PG-13…). US usage is "what is it rated"; other languages are untouched.

### Fixes
- **The pause screen's row icons can be themed away.** Each metadata row label starts with an emoji ("📅 Year"); it is now wrapped in `<i class="pause-row-icon" aria-hidden="true">` so a theme can hide the glyph while keeping the text; the progress strip's "⏳ Remaining" label gets the same wrapper. Nothing changes without such a theme.

### Features
- **A settings gear in the header, next to the notifications bell.** The gear that opens MonWUI's settings lived only in the hero's provider strip, so a theme that hides that strip, or any page without the slider, left the F2 hotkey as the only way in. The header button mounts the way the bell does (MUI and legacy headers), follows the "Show settings link" option, and opens the MonWUI tab. F2 still works.

### Fixes
- **The About tab shows the installed version.** `config.version` was the constant "v4.0.0.7" inherited from ParticularFlix, so About and the update check reported 4.0.0.7 whatever was installed. The version now comes from the `?v=` stamp the plugin puts on its own module URLs.

### Features
- **A fallback clip when a card has nothing to preview.** Drop `preview-fallback.mp4` (card-shaped, 2:3) and optionally `preview-fallback-wide.mp4` (16:9) into the plugin's `custom` folder and the hover preview plays that clip, looping and muted with no speaker button, whenever a title has no trailer and no playable video (an empty or not-yet-downloaded series, trailer-only mode on a title without a trailer) and whenever a YouTube embed reports an error (removed, private, embedding off, region-locked). Without the files the "trailer not available" note shows as before. The custom folder now serves `.mp4`/`.webm` (never injected), answers `HEAD`, and honours `Range` requests for videos.

### Fixes
- **Plugin settings can be saved again.** The settings page loaded and saved the configuration without sending the user's token, so the server answered "401 Authentication required" to every Save (and to the Env panel); the page's own token helper was only used for publishing user settings. Every call from the settings page now carries the token (falling back to the token jellyfin-web keeps in local storage when the dashboard does not expose `ApiClient`).
- **A title with nothing to preview keeps its hover card.** When a card had no trailer and no playable video (a series that has only missing or not-yet-downloaded episodes, or trailer-only mode on a title without a trailer), the preview closed the card right after opening it, so it looked as if the hover did not work. The card now stays, with its backdrop, details and buttons and a "trailer not available" note; an error while resolving the preview no longer takes an opened card away either.
- **A series preview plays the episode you would play next**, not a random one: the one you are part-way through, else the first unwatched, else the first. Missing ("virtual") episodes, which have no media, are never picked; they were, and left the preview empty.

### Fixes
- **A slow-starting YouTube preview is no longer muted by mistake.** 4.0.0.81's sound check gave the player 0.7 s after it reported ready before treating it as blocked by the browser and muting it until the next click; a normal start took up to 0.6 s on the bench, so a slightly slow one would have lost its sound. The check now waits up to 3.5 s while the player is still starting, and only acts when it is paused or still muted after that.

### Fixes
- **YouTube trailer previews start on a freshly loaded page.** Browsers only allow autoplay with sound once you have clicked or typed somewhere on the page; before that, a YouTube embed asked to start unmuted just showed its play button, so after a reload every hover preview waited for one click. With the sound setting on, such a preview now starts muted and is unmuted the moment the browser allows it: at once when it does, otherwise on your first click or key anywhere. The same fallback covers the film-itself preview, whose `play()` a browser can refuse in the same situation.
- **A closed preview can no longer block its card.** A theme rule that forces the preview's display (the Lumen theme's card rule did) kept the closed preview in the page, invisible, on top of the poster it had opened from, so that card could not be hovered or clicked again until another preview opened. The closed preview now ignores the pointer whatever the theme does; Lumen also fixes its rule.
- **The hero no longer moves the page when its slideshow starts over.** When the last slide finished and the hero rebuilt itself for a new round, the page was scrolled back to the top and, during the rebuild, the rows jumped by the hero's height. Rebuilding now keeps your scroll position and holds the hero's place.
- **Lighter previews for very high-bitrate films.** The preview of a film with AC3/E-AC3/DTS/TrueHD audio copied H.264 video as it is; for a Blu-ray remux that meant streaming 25 Mbit/s (and writing about 1 GB to the transcode cache in ten seconds) for a thumbnail-sized preview. Video above 8 Mbit/s is now scaled to the preview size instead.

### Fixes
- **Card hover previews have sound for films with AC3, E-AC3, DTS or TrueHD audio.** When a title has no trailer, the hover plays the film itself, and it asked Jellyfin for the original file untouched; browsers cannot decode those audio formats, so the picture played with no sound. When the track that would play is not browser-safe, the preview now asks for that track as stereo AAC (H.264 video is copied as it is, anything else is scaled down to the preview size) and starts where the preview always started. Films with AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis or FLAC audio still play the original file, at no cost to the server.

### Fixes
- The hero's info line no longer ends with a stray separator for titles that have no production country.

### Card hover
- **The trailer preview remembers your sound choice.** Mute or unmute it (or move its volume slider) on one card and every following preview starts the same way, including after a reload. Before, the mute button only affected the card you were on, so the next hover started with sound again. An explicit choice now wins over the "start muted" setting; the volume limit still applies. The details popup and studio trailer previews use the same memory.
- **Themes can make the preview take the card's own shape.** With `--monwui-hover-shape: card` (and optionally `--monwui-hover-card-scale`, default 1.3) set on `:root`, the preview opens as a larger copy of the hovered card, centred on it and clear of the top bar, with the class `video-preview-modal--card` (`--card-wide` for 16:9 cards) for styling. Without the variable the preview is unchanged. The Lumen theme uses it.

### New in the details popup
- **Choose the audio track and subtitles before you press Play.** When a film or episode has more than one audio track, an Audio dropdown sits under the buttons; when it has subtitles, a Subtitles dropdown (with Off) sits next to it. Each opens on the track Jellyfin would pick for you (your language settings, or the tracks you chose last time for this title), and Play Now plays what you chose. Items with one audio track and no subtitles look as before.
- **Add to playlist**, next to Go to Page: lists your Jellyfin playlists (audio-only playlists are left out) and can create a new playlist with the title in it.

### Fixes
- **Hero backdrops appear as soon as the slider rotates on its own.** With slide animations on, a slide change hides the incoming backdrop and waits for its image to load before fading it in. The next slides' images are preloaded in the background, so they had already loaded and nothing faded them in: the backdrop stayed invisible until the mouse moved over the hero or the slider moved on. A backdrop that is already loaded now fades in straight away.

### Fixes
- **The player header shows the title you are watching, not the previous one.** When a video streams without its item id in the URL (an HLS stream while transcoding), the header's logo, star rating, tomato score and age rating came from the first favourite button in the page. Jellyfin keeps earlier pages hidden in the page, so that could be the previous title's player or item page; it showed most often after starting something from the MonWUI popup on the home page. The header now only reads a page that is showing, the player page first. When it falls back to the server's session list, it prefers this browser's own session over another device's.

### Faster on TVs
- **TV web browsers no longer load any part of MonWUI.** With "Disable MonWUI for TV web clients" on, TVs used to get the full MonWUI page header (an import map, about 96 module preloads and the boot scripts) and then download each file empty. That was about 100 extra requests on every page load. TVs now get Jellyfin's page with the MonWUI block removed, plus the small remote-focus helper written inline. On a TV-speed test the home page shows its first card in half the time (2.5 s to 1.2 s) with half the requests. Desktop and phone browsers are unchanged.

### Fixes
- **The hero slider and custom rows no longer disappear when you click the server logo.** The logo links to `#/`, which Jellyfin immediately turns back into `#/home` while building a brand-new home page. MonWUI saw the same address as before and did nothing, so the slider and its rows stayed with the discarded page, and "My Media" moved up under the header. MonWUI now notices when the home page itself is replaced, and rebuilds the slider and rows in your saved order.
- **The settings button on "Who's watching" opens its menu right there.** It used to close the chooser and open Jellyfin's user menu at the top-left of the home page. The same entries (Profile, Settings, Dashboard and Metadata Manager for admins, Quick Connect, Sign out) now open under the gear, inside the chooser. Escape, clicking elsewhere, or the gear again closes just the menu.
- **The Runtime Status on the plugin page no longer looks like an error.** An empty Script Directory is the normal setup: the plugin uses its built-in scripts, which update with it. The card now shows "Script source: Built into the plugin" and "Custom script directory: Not used", instead of "Configured: No", "Directory exists: No" and a yellow "Using embedded assets: Yes". The Script Directory hint now says to leave it empty.

### Fixes
- **The update check now watches this fork.** MonWUI's built-in update notice, its "update available" links and the GitHub link on the settings page pointed at the ParticularFlix repository, so the plugin could suggest their releases, which do not include this fork's changes. They now point at github.com/Zigerus/Jellyfin-MonWUI-Plugin. The link to the original G-grbz project is kept.

Fixes the three known issues listed for 4.0.0.71. Settings are kept.

### Fixes
- **No more page reload after logging in.** Jellyfin's login screen does not reload the page, but MonWUI saw the new user as a profile switch the first time it saved a setting and reloaded the freshly loaded home page. It now loads the signed-in user's own settings the moment the login completes, before the home page appears. Switching profiles and signing out still reload, as before.
- **No more 401 errors on the login page.** The parental PIN status and studio hub visibility checks ran before anyone was signed in. They now wait for a signed-in user.
- **No more "getScrollSlider is not a function" with a custom home section order.** Jellyfin adds a row of scroll arrows each time a row is attached to the page and never removes the old one. When MonWUI moved a row into your chosen order, the row ended up with a second set of arrows wired to the wrong element. MonWUI now waits until a row's arrows are ready, removes them before moving the row, and lets Jellyfin build exactly one set again.

First release of the Zigerus fork (github.com/Zigerus/Jellyfin-MonWUI-Plugin). Same code as ParticularFlix 4.0.0.7, plus the changes below. Same plugin GUID, so it upgrades any JMSFusion install in place, and your settings are kept.

### New
- **Turn MonWUI off for TV web browsers** (Plugins, then JMSFusion, then "Disable MonWUI for TV web clients"). TV browsers whose User-Agent matches the pattern get the stock Jellyfin web UI: the slider and modules are served empty, and a small focus helper keeps the remote working. The default pattern `Web0S|SmartTV|WebAppManager|Tizen` covers LG webOS and Samsung Tizen. The setting is **off by default**. Desktop, phone and native apps are not affected.

### Build
- Built against the Jellyfin 12.0.0 packages, so the `12.0.0.0` minimum this release declares is the real minimum (4.0.0.7 compiled against 12.3.0).
- Releases are now built by GitHub Actions and published to this fork's own plugin repository: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zigerus/Jellyfin-MonWUI-Plugin/main/manifest.json`.

### Known issues (found on Jellyfin 12.4.0, to be fixed next)
- The page reloads once right after you log in.
- The login page shows two harmless 401 errors in the browser console.
- With a custom home section order, the console can show `getScrollSlider is not a function`.
